discovery: The jamming transition as a unifying framework for the rigidity of disordered matter
subfield: Statistical physics of soft and disordered matter
motivation: Liu and Nagel proposed that foams, emulsions, granular packings and colloidal and molecular glasses acquire rigidity through a common jamming transition, organised in a single phase diagram of density, temperature and load. Their work, with O'Hern and collaborators, identified Point J: an isostatic critical point with power-law scaling of the pressure, the shear modulus and the excess contact number, a plateau of anomalous soft vibrational modes, and a diverging length scale. This picture turned a messy many-body problem into a clear physical one. It explains the boson peak, the anomalous elasticity of amorphous bodies and where plastic rearrangements occur, and it links microscopic simulation to experiments across physics, chemistry, materials science and biology. It laid the foundation for later mean-field theories of glasses and for the design of mechanical metamaterials. It now shapes how we understand the mechanics, flow and failure of all amorphous solids.
